answer.evidence: radon/raw.py:72-79 defines `_find(tokens, token, value)`. It iterates `enumerate(reversed(tokens))` to find the last (rightmost) tokens whose type and text both match. If nothing matches, it raises `ValueError('(token, value) pair not found')` at line 79. Review focus: (1) confirm the index conversion from the reversed enumeration back to a forward index (`len(tokens) - index - 1` or similar) is correct, including off-by-one on single-element and empty lists. (2) Check that callers handle the ValueError. The raw.py `analyze`/logical-line code around line 212 is the main consumer and also raises SyntaxError. (3) Check the tests in radon/tests/test_raw.py, around line 49, which use pytest.raises(ValueError). complexity.py:41 has an unrelated ValueError for negative complexity, so it needs only a brief check. metrics.py gets a secondary pass for any token-scanning helpers that may reuse the same pattern. visitors.py gets a brief check that it has no duplicate implementation.
